newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen firm next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen firm next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are likely to remain firm in the next trading week in line with the international prices, dealers said on Saturday.
"Last week the local market ended up and this trend is likely to continue as the vegoil rates in international market are firm," dealer Naeem Ashraf of Jaleel Brothers Ltd said.
Dealers said vegoil stocks rose to an estimated 159,000 tonnes last week from 155,000 tonnes on February 1. The market was closed last week due to Eid-ul Fitr holidays.

RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to an estimated 115,000 tonnes compared to 118,000. Soybean oil and Sunflower oil stocks rose to an estimated 34,000 tonnes from about 27,000 tonnes, while the Ghee Corporation of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks remained steady at around 10,000 tonnes.
Wawasan Courage is discharging around 22,095 tonnes of palm oil at the Port Qasim, while Mayra around 12,000 tonnes of soyabean oil at the Karachi port.
Cielo Di-Serona, with around 6,000 tonnes of soyabean oil, and Global Mars and Bow Princes with 6,500 and 10,000 of palm oil respectively were at high seas.
Sunga Chenterawasih and Manado were loading 25,000 and 10,000 tonnes of palm oil for Pakistan at Malaysian Port.
